INTRODUCTION TO GGGI

The Global Green Growth Institute (GGGI) is a treaty-based international, inter-governmental organization dedicated to supporting and promoting strong, inclusive and sustainable economic growth in developing countries and emerging economies. To learn more please visit about GGGI web page.
Application Deadline: Shown in the bottom of the page. All applications must be submitted by 10:00 PM (KST) on the closing date.
Position Grade: G8
Position Scale: Country Scale
End date of appointment: 31 December 2028
Salary: National
Position Summary

GGGI has been assigned by the Ministry of Finance, Directorate General of Financial Sector Stability and Development, which serves as the NDA Secretariat to implement the core functions of the NDA GCF in Indonesia, as the Delivery Partner for the Green Climate Fund (GCF) – for the implementation of “Accelerating Climate Finance Access and Delivery through Institutional Reforms in Indonesia (CLAP)” (the “Project”), funded by the GCF Readiness and Preparatory Support Program. This project will build on and complement the results obtain from the previous three GCF Readiness grants implemented in 2019-2020 (Readiness I), 2020-2022 (Readiness II), and 2023-2026 (Readiness III) with GGGI’s support.

The Climate Investment Officer will be responsible for managing determined activities of the project, particularly in identifying, assessing, and prioritize potential projects and programs for inclusion in the national climate finance pipeline, development and management of the project pipeline by providing technical support to nominated and candidate DAEs in preparing high quality concept notes that meet GCF standards, align with the GCF Country Programme Document (CPD) priorities, and are investment ready for submission to the GCF and other international climate finance mechanisms.

The Climate Investment Officer will actively in charge in development of climate investment projects in Indonesia, including facilitate the preparation of technical assessment, feasibility studies, and other project preparation activities required. The Officer will also be responsible to provide technical assistance and capacity building to relevant stakeholders, including nominated/candidate DAEs, and others. The Climate Investment Officer will report directly to the Senior Climate Finance Officer as the Project Manager and will work three four days per week at the Ministry of Finance office (project office). On other days, s/he will be working from the GGGI Jakarta office. S/he should be willing to travel.
Purpose

Conduct analysis for potential climate related projects and programmes for includion the national climate finance pipeline, considering climate impact, investment potential, implementation readiness, and alignment with GCF investment criteria.

Lead the development and management of the project pipeline by providing technical support to nominated/candidate DAEs and other relevant entities in preparing at least two high-quality concept notes that align with the country priorities and are investment-ready for submission to the GCF and other international climate finance mechanisms.

Monitor and manage the progression of pipeline projects from concept to funding by providing technical assistance to relevant entities in preparing and submitting at least one high-quality funding proposal to the GCF or other international climate finance sources such as Adaptation Funds, Global Environmental Fund, etc.

Engaging and coordinate with public, private, and civil society organizations to increase their capacity in developing project pipeline in accordance with the GCF standards and criteria, as well as align with the Country priorities.

Coordinate and engage with international AEs and other potential implementing entities to facilitate the preparation of technical assessments, feasibility studies, and other project preparation activities required.
Engagement
Primarily support the Sr. Climate Finance Officer for CLAP in engagement with the public and private sector at national and sub-national levels, NGOs/CSOs, and other relevant stakeholders.

Collaborate with professional experts, research centers, and development partners in conducting pre-feasibility and feasibility studies required to develop and/or implement projects in specific sectors.
Provide support to the GGGI Investment Team at country level in the development of the GGGI project portfolio and carry out other assignment in line with GGGI’s mandate and targets for Indonesia.

Work as the key expert to relevant stakeholders, strengthen the stakeholders’ capacity and provide necessary assistance and guidance to improve green/climate projects initiated by International and National DAEs. Ensure effective and efficient delivery of related project deliverables.
Support the monitoring of project implementation. Collaborate with other units and divisions at GGGI globally and in Indonesia, particularly those related to GCF program/projects.
Collaborate closely with GGGI Indonesia’s Investment Unit to support and assist in resource mobilization and investment mobilization.
Delivery

Lead the implementation of Project Outcome 2.2, focusing on the development of investment-grade concept notes for climate change adaptation and mitigation initiatives, ensuring alignment with national priorities and international climate finance standards, including technical studies or pre- and feasibility studies, to strengthen project pipelines and support the development of bankable funding proposals for submission to potential climate finance sources, such as GCF, GEF, or AF.
Initiate and lead relevant workshops, dialogues, focus group discussions, and consultations with key national and subnational stakeholders from both public and private sector/financial institutions.

Deliver the identification, assessment, and prioritization of potential projects and programmes for the national climate finance pipeline, ensuring that selected initiatives are supported by robust technical assessments, demonstrate strong climate impact and investment potential, are sufficiently mature for implementation, and are aligned with national priorities and GCF/other climate finance investment criteria.High-quality concept notes that align with the country priorities and are investment-ready for submission to the GCF and other international climate finance mechanisms.
Organize the delivery of Project Outcome 2.2 in tight deadlines and working with the project team, as well as manage a small team, including consultants and interns.
Support in developing various documents or portions of documents in support of project design, institutional capacity building, and internal/external program reporting.
Uphold GGGI’s values.
REQUIREMENS
QUALIFICATION
Master’s degree relevant to climate finance, sustainable finance, international finance, environmental economics, development economics, and/or environment finance.
Minimum 5 (five) years of relevant professional experience in related to green finance project development and management, with proven experience on climate and sustainable finance.
A good track record of working on project development, investment processes, banking and non-banking sector, and public sector finance is desirable.
Demonstrate knowledge of GCF framework and policies, modalities and procedures, including reporting requirements and guidelines.

Strong experience and technical knowledge of climate change mitigation and adaptation, and climate finance landscape of Indonesia, international climate finance sources, climate projects development, green growth, and sustainable development.
Experience with the development and structuring of climate investment projects and financial instruments in for climate-related projects.
Previous experience with the management of donor-funded activities.
Ability to work effectively with people from diverse cultural and professional backgrounds.
Excellent English and Indonesian oral and written communication skills, including public speaking.
FUNCTIONAL
Proven ability to provide high-quality advice on project development and investments on climate change.
Proven analytical, problem-solving, and strategic skills.
Demonstrated ability to build collaborative working relationships with government counterparts.
Demonstrated capacity to facilitate in-depth, outcome oriented, stakeholder dialogues.
Excellent interpersonal, stakeholder engagement and consensus-building skills.
Ability to foster strong relationships with key government agencies and ensure ownership of program’s input.
Ability to write concise and clear reports and meeting minutes and to file them effectively and develop and maintain the GGGI database accordingly.
Ability to perform in demanding atmosphere and self-motivate to produce quality results in timely manner.
CORPORATE
Understand and actively support GGGI’s mission, vision and values.
Promote an organizational culture of trust, transparency, respect and partnership.
Excels at problem solving, asks questions and seeks support when needed, easily shares information and knowledge with others both internally as externally.
Manage emotions and stress positively, build rapport and resolves conflict easily.
Strong ability to work independently and/or remotely, while maintaining productivity.
Work Conditions
Climate Investment Officer is an G8 grade level in GGGI’s National salary scale. Determination of base salary is subject to candidate's experience, academic background and internal equity.
GGGI provides 15% of base salary towards retirement plan/long-term savings, 27 days of annual leave, and private health insurance that covers dental and vision.

GGGI is committed to providing a work environment that is sufficiently flexible to accommodate diverse life-cycle challenges and assist Staff members to achieve a better balance between work and personal/family commitments, thus ensuring high performance, long-term productivity, and well-being of Staff members.

The chosen candidate is expected to be based in Jakarta, Indonesia, and will report to the Senior Climate Finance Officer of the GGGI Indonesia, serves as the Readiness Program Manager (also based in Jakarta).
This is a national position and does not include relocation benefits.
PROJECT INTRODUCTION

GGGI supports the Government of Indonesia (GoI) under the joint GoI-GGGI Green Indonesia Future Initiative Program (GIFT, “the Program”). The Program aims to demonstrate that green investments can become the norm both for investors and planners, ultimately improving the quality of economic development for more environmental sustainability and social inclusion. Through the Program, GGGI collaborates with the Ministry of Development Planning (BAPPENAS) as program host, the Coordinating Ministry of Economic Affairs, Ministry of Finance, Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources, Ministry of Environment, Ministry of Forestry, PT Sarana Multi Infrastruktur (“PT SMI”) , Indonesia Environment Fund (IEF), and others.

In October 2026, the Readiness Proposal for Indonesia, titled Accelerating Climate Finance Access and Delivery through Institutional Reforms in Indonesia has been approved by the GCF Secretariat. Funded by the Green Climate Fund (GCF), this 4-years GCF Multiyear Readiness Program will help to strengthen Indonesia’s institutional capacity, governance framework, and strategic planning to mobilize and manage climate finance effectively. Building on lessons from previous Readiness Phases, current program addresses systemic gaps that hinder Indonesia’s ability to access and deploy climate finance at scale, while aligning with national climate priorities and the GCF 2024-2027 Readiness Strategy. It consists of a range of activities with the objective of achieving three main readiness outcomes which will directly contribute to the GCF Readiness Outcomes under the 2024-2027 strategy:
Outcome 1: Strengthened NDA capacity and strategic frameworks for NDC, NAP, and LTS implementation.
Outcome 2: Development of four high-quality concept notes aligned with NCFS programming targets.
Outcome 3: Enhanced knowledge-sharing and regional collaboration to scale climate finance innovation.

Child protection – GGGI is committed to child protection, irrespective of whether any specific area of work involves direct contact with children. GGGI’s Child Protection Policy is written in accordance with the Convention on the Rights of the Child.
